8200.full: 1. to have gone before, be the first , (Thucydides) 2. to have advanced , πρ. ἐς βαθὺ τῆς ἡλικίας (Aristophanes Comicus); εἰς τοῦτο προήκειν to have come to this pass, (Demosthenes Orator); of Time, τῆς ἡμέρας προηκούσας (Plutarch) 3. to reach beyond , τῆς ἄρκυος (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8204.full: πρωτο-κλυτία, -ας, ἡ the chief place at table (see Swete, Mk., l.with): Mat.23:6, Mrk.12:39, Luk.14:7-8 20:46.† (AS)

8207.full: πρωτοστάτης, -ου, ὁ (πρῶτος, ἵστημι) [in LXX: Job.15:24 AB * ;] prop., of soldiers, one who stands first, one in the front rank (Thuc., Xen.); hence, metaphorically, a leader: Act.24:5.† (AS)

8208.g: to give a right of first-born
8208.full: to give a right of first-born

s: one who exacts payment, a collector
8211.full: πράκτωρ, -ορος, ὁ (πράσσω), [in LXX: Isa.3:12 (נָגַשׁ) * ;] __1. (poët.) one who does or accomplishes. __2. In Athens, one who exacts payment, a collector; hence, generally (frequently in π., see Deiss., BS, 154), a court officer: Luk.12:58.† (AS)

8217.full: 1. a putting to, application of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 2. an adding, addition , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

8219.full: 1. at hand, ready , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ . . ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is easy , with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 3. of persons, ready to do, with infinitive, (Sophocles Tragicus); with dative, πρ. τῇ φυγῇ ready for flight, (Euripides) 4. adverb -ρως, off-hand, readily , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

8220.full: 1. a prince, ruler, lord, chief , of Hiero, (Pindar); of Zeus, (Pindar) 2. at Athens, a Prytanis or President : the πρυτάνεις were a committee of 50, chosen by lot from each of the 10 φυλαί, so that each set formed 1/10 part of the βουλή or Council of 500; out of these 50 πρυτάνεις one was chosen by lot as chief-president ἐπιστάτης); he chose 9 πρόεδρο; and the real business was in the hands of this smaller body, with a secretary γραμματεύς); added.—;The φυλή which first entered office every year was determined by lot; and their term of office πρυτανεία); was about five weeks. During this time all treaties and public acts ran in their name, in this form: Ἀκαμαντὶς φυλὴ, ἐπρυτάνευε, Φαίνιππος ἐγραμμάτευε, Νικιάδης ἐπεστάτει the Tribe Acamantis were the Presidency, Phaenippus the Secretary, Niciades the Chief-president, (Thucydides) (ML)

8221.full: 1. lately, just now , Lat. nuper, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 2. the day before yesterday , οὐ χθές, ἀλλὰ πρ. (Thucydides); πρώην τε καὶ χθές till yesterday or the day before , i. e. till very lately , (Herdotus Historicus); so, χθές τε καὶ πρώην (Aristophanes Comicus); πρώην καὶ χθές (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

8224.full: 1. a stumble, trip, false step , (Theognis Elegiacus) 2. a failure, misfortune, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. from πτάξ (ML)

8232.full: πυρετός, -οῦ, ὁ (πῦρ) [in LXX: Deu.28:22 (קַדַּחַת) * ;] a fever: Mat.8:15, Mrk.1:31, Luk.4:39, Jhn.4:52, Act.28:8; π. μέγας, a high fever: Luk.4:38 (on the technical phrase here, see MM, xxii).† (AS)

8233.full: giving forth fire:—; τὰ πυροβόλα bolts or arrows tipped with fire , (Plutarch) (ML)

s: the priest who kept the sacrificial fire
8236.full: 1. fire-bearing , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of lightning, (Pindar):—; πυρφόροι ὀϊστοί arrows with combustibles tied to them , (Thucydides) 2. in special senses, 3. epithet of Zeus in reference to his lightnings, (Sophocles Tragicus); of Demeter, in reference to the torches used by her worshippers, (Euripides); of Artemis, (Sophocles Tragicus); but θεὸς πυρφόρος the fire-bearing god, the god who produces plague or fever , (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. ὁ πυρφόρος, in the Lacedaemonian army, was the priest who kept the sacrificial fire , which was never allowed to go out, (Xenophon Historicus); hence proverbial of a total defeat, ἔδεε δὲ μηδὲ πυρφόρον περιγενέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

8244.full: 1. near, hard by, close , with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 3. absolute, χριμφθεὶς πέλας (Odyssey by Homer); π. στείχειν, παρεῖναι, στῆναι [variant datesTragica Adespota 4. οἱ πέλας (i.e. ὄντες); one's neighbours , (Thucydides), etc.: hence one's fellow-creatures, all men , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: to be poor in, have need of
to work at, prepare, get ready
8246.full: 1. Dep., used in present and imperfect : 2. intransitive to work for one's daily bread ; generally, to toil, work, labour , (Homer) 3. to be poor or needy , Solon , (Euripides), etc. 4. with genitive to be poor in, have need of , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 5. transitive to work at, prepare, get ready , δαῖτα πένοντο (Odyssey by Homer); τί σε χρὴ ταῦτα πένεσθα; (Odyssey by Homer) (ML)

8248.full: 1. of fruit, cooked by the sun, ripe, mellow , Lat. mitis, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 2. metaphorically in vocative, mostly as a term of endearment, kind, gentle , ὦ πέπον my good friend , (Iliad by Homer); κριὲ πέπον my pet ram, (Odyssey by Homer);—; in bad sense, soft, weak , (Iliad by Homer); ὦ πέπονες ye weaklings , (Iliad by Homer): —; μόχθος πέπων softened pain, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.: with dative, ἐχθροῖς π. gentle to one's foes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

8249.full: a perch for fowls to roost at night, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) derivation uncertain (ML)

8251.full: an ape, monkey , (Aristophanes Comicus); as feminine, πίθηκος μήτηρ (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor):—;of persons, an ape, jackanapes , (Aristophanes Comicus) derivation uncertain (ML)

8252.full: πιθός, see: πειθός. πειθός (πιθός, WH), -ή, -όν (πείθω), = cl. πιθανός, persuasive: 1Co.2:4 (not found elsewhere).† (AS)

8253.full: 1. grass, herb , (Homer), etc.; ποία Μηδική, Lat. herba Medica, sainfoin or lucerne , (Aristophanes Comicus) 2. the grass , i. e. a grassy place , plat., (Xenophon Historicus) 3. in Poets, of Time, τέσσαρας πόας four grasses , i. e. summers , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

8255.lxx: in LXX: Da, LXX TH Dan.1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה) *
8255.full: πόσις, -εως, ἡ (πίνω), [in LXX: Da, LXX TH Dan.1:10 (מִשְׁתֶּה) * ;] __1. prop., drinking: Rom.14:17, Col.2:16 (see Lft.; ICC, in l). __2. = πόμα, drink: Jhn.6:55 (cf. βρῶσις).† (AS)

8257.full: 1. white-rump , the name of a kind of antelope, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. the white-tailed eagle, the erne , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

8269.full: 1. a man's pack, baggage , αὐτόφορτος οἰκείᾳ σαγῇ, i. e. carrying his own baggage, (Aeschulus Tragicus): generally, harness, equipment , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. = σάγμα II, a pack-saddle , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

8277.full: σεμνότης, -ητος, ἡ (σεμνός), [in LXX: 2Ma.3:12 * ;] gravity: 1Ti.2:2 3:4 (Vg. eastitas, cf. Soph., Lex., and Zorell, see word), Tit.2:7.† (AS)

s: the trunk of an old olive-tree
8281.full: 1. a pen, fold , for lambs, kids, calves, (Homer); ς. δράκοντος the dragon's den , (Euripides) 2. a sacred enclosure, chapel, shrine , (Sophocles Tragicus) 3. a sepulchre, burial-place , (Simonides Lyricus) 4. the trunk of an old olive-tree , (Lysias Orator) (ML)

8282.full: σημειόω, -ῶ (σημεῖον), [in LXX: Psa.4:6 (נָשָׂא)* ;] to mark, note. Mid., to note for oneself: 2Th.3:14 (frequently in π.; see ICC, M, Th., in l).† (AS)

8285.full: 1. to have strength or might, be strong or mighty , (Sophocles Tragicus); σθ. χερί, ποσί to be strong in hand, in foot, (Sophocles Tragicus); σθένοντος ἐν πλούτῳ (Sophocles Tragicus); τοσοῦτον σθένει (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅσονπερ ἂν σθένῃ (Sophocles Tragicus); οἱ κάτω σθένοντες they who have power below, (Euripides) 2. with infinitive to have strength or power to do, be able , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

8293.full: 1. grain, corn: food made from grain, bread , ποιεῖσθαι σιτία ἀπὸ ὀλυρέων to feed off spelt, (Herdotus Historicus) 2. generally, food, victuals, provisions , (Herdotus Historicus); σιτία ἡμερῶν τριῶν three days' provision , of soldiers, (Aristophanes Comicus); σιτία καὶ ποτά meat and drink, (Plato Philosophus) 3. τἀν Πρυτανείῳ σιτία public maintenance in the Prytaneum, (Aristophanes Comicus); compare σίτησις. 4. rarely food for dogs, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

8294.full: 1. silence , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; σιωπὴν ποιεῖν (Xenophon Historicus); ἦν ς. there was a hush or calm , (Sophocles Tragicus) 2. the habit of silence , (Demosthenes Orator) 3. dative σιωπῇ as adverb, in silence , (Homer), attic derivation uncertain (ML)
